title: Adaptive Mixbench: multi-variant kernel selection and prefill/decode cadence harness
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
Build a next-generation benchmarking harness (Adaptive Mixbench) that evaluates runtime kernel selection policies and prefill/decode scheduling strategies across a curated workload matrix. This harness will produce deterministic 'golden' baselines for kernel mix, latency quantiles, decode-step tail behavior, and memory-pressure fingerprints used by CI perf gates and rollout decisions.

Goals and scope:
- Support multi-variant runs (kernel candidates, attention kernels, quantization modes) in a single coordinated job so we can measure interactions (e.g., kernel X + attention-opt Y + decode cadence Z).
- Introduce a prefill/decode cadence simulator to reproduce bursty chat workloads and streaming scenarios; capture per-token latency distributions and KV-cache hit profiles.
- Produce reproducible golden artifacts (seeded workloads + deterministic runtime flags) stored in the benchmark bucket for CI comparison.
- Define CI perf gates (p50/p95/p99 thresholds per route + allowed regressions for token throughput and memory footprint) with automatic PR annotations and optional rollout block.
- Integrate with perf dashboards (Grafana) and the benchmarking orchestration service (bench-orch) so infra and SRE can schedule nightly and on-demand golden runs.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- New harness runs end-to-end for 3 canonical workloads (long-context assistant, short Q/A, streaming-chat) and produces JSON golden artifacts.
- CI perf gate detects a regress >3% p95 latency or >5% token-cost increase and leaves machine-readable annotation on PRs.
- Dashboard shows kernel-selection breakdown (percentage of requests routed to each kernel) and decode-step tail plotted per 1k steps.
- Latency measurements stable within 1% across 5 repeated golden runs (same seed).

Design notes / approach:
- Workload matrix: canonical prompts from eval-corpus (long-assistant-16k, qna-2k, streaming-500) × model variants (gptx-13B-int8, gptx-70B-q4) × kernel candidates (fast-matmul-v1, patched-matmul-v2, attention-opt-l1) × prefill/decode cadence presets (batch-prefill-heavy, streaming-low-latency, hybrid-prefill-decode).
- Each run will record: per-request start/end timestamps, per-token decode latency, kernel invocation histogram, memory high-water mark, KV cache hit ratio, GPU SM occupancy (sampled), and power-profile tags when available.
- Determinism: seed PRNGs at workload generation and fix runtime RNG flags; use small synthetic traces for golden baselines to avoid flaky public corpora.
- Storage: golden artifacts stored under gs://redwood-bench/goldens/adaptive-mixbench/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<commit-hash>/ with manifest.json linking runs to kernel flags.

CI integration and gates:
- Implement compare script that runs on CI runner (or bench-orch) which: fetches nearest golden by model+workload, computes delta metrics, and returns a JSON result.
- Gate logic (proposed): block PR if p95 latency for any route increases by >3% AND p99 increases by >5% OR token-cost (tokens/sec normalized) decreases by >7%. Minor regressions (p95 1-3%) will annotate but not block.
- Add auto-commenter and presubmit that attaches a link to the benchmark diff and the dashboard snapshot.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype harness and run locally for the three canonical workloads (2 weeks).
2) Run nightly golden jobs on bench-orch and validate reproducibility (1 week).
3) Implement CI compare script and gate behavior behind a feature flag in CI (2 weeks).
4) Gradual enforcement—start as annotating-only for 2 cycles, then enable blocking for P0 PRs.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Making goldens synthetic reduces representativeness; mitigate by keeping separate 'field' traces for non-blocking monitoring.
- Running large matrix can be expensive; use smart sampling and submit heavy runs to dedicated capacity windows.
- Determinism vs. fidelity: locking kernels and flags may hide non-deterministic regressions; we will keep a 'wild-run' nightly job without deterministic flags.

Artifacts and links:

- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2876 
- Bench-orch job definition: https://gitlab.redwood.ai/bench-orch/-/blob/main/jobs/adaptive-mixbench.yaml
- Golden dashboard (Grafana snapshot): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/adaptive-mixbench-goldens
- Storage manifest example: gs://redwood-bench/goldens/adaptive-mixbench/example-manifest.json
